# `aitbc agent-comm send`

Send a message from a sender to a receiver agent via the coordinator. Maps to ``POST /api/v1/agent/messages/send`` — the coordinator routes the envelope to the receiver's inbox (and across chains via its routing table).

## Usage

```bash
aitbc agent-comm send [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--sender-id` | text | — | yes | The Sender id. |
| `--receiver-id` | text | — | yes | The Receiver id. |
| `--message-type` | text | — | yes | The Message type. |
| `--chain-id` | text | — | yes | The Chain id. |
| `--payload` | text | `{}` | no | JSON payload string |
| `--target-chain` | text | — | no | Target chain for cross-chain messages |
| `--priority` | integer | `5` | no | Message priority (1-10) |
| `--ttl` | integer | `3600` | no | Time to live in seconds |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet signing the message envelope (default: $AITBC_DEFAULT_WALLET); must be the sender's bound identity |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc agent-comm send --sender-id <sender_id> --receiver-id <receiver_id> --message-type <message_type> --chain-id <chain_id>
```
